Meta.title: VEXILLA — A Visual Archive of Flags
Meta.description: An editorial journey through the histories, colors and symbols behind national flags and their subdivisions.

Hero.lede: An editorial archive of what pulses behind every band, star and crest. Explore nations, traverse states, discover colors that changed meaning and symbols that outlived empires.

Manifesto.quote: Flags don't decorate countries — they compress centuries into four or five chromatic gestures.

cards.title: Form is argument
cards.body: Every geometric division carries doctrine: horizontal bands were born of revolution, cantons celebrate union, triangles isolate guiding ideas.

cards.title: Color is memory
cards.body: Greens that once meant faith became forest. Reds once monarchic became laborers'. Every palette is an archaeological layer.

cards.title: Symbol is resistance
cards.body: Stars mark states, suns mark peoples, animals mark lineages. Each element survived a contest of narratives.

Archive.title: Choose where to begin.
Archive.lede: Filter by continent, era of adoption or dominant color. Each card opens a full visual dossier.

Chronicle.title: Four centuries in cloth.
Chronicle.lede: From the Thirteen Colonies to post-colonial flags — drag to traverse.

Palette.lede: Hover a color to reveal the nations that adopted it and what it means in each context.

Palette.restrictedText: Security protocols block direct pixel access for this source. Use the official archival metadata below.

Footer.tagline: An editorial archive of vexillology, culture and design. An independent project — all flags belong to the peoples they represent.
